biography.value:
Lady Aurelian Corvinarus, the Orange Heir

Lady Aurelian Corvinarus is the mistress of the Feywild reflection of the manor, a being who presents herself as a delicate fey noblewoman while concealing a nature far older and more dangerous than her porcelain appearance suggests. She is the "Orange Heir" referenced in Perrius Anamatar's warnings and Hjumpik's visions—the inheritor of a bloodline that traces back to 988 BF, when an orange-robed figure cut their palm over a screaming dragon egg and bound the Corvinarus family to powers that have sustained them through centuries of dimensional instability.

The party first encountered Aurelian in the overgrown Master Bedroom of the Feywild manor on Highsun 26, where she played the role of a delicate, overwhelmed hostess desperately trying to manage an eternal party that had spiraled beyond her control. She asked Hjumpik and his companions to remove the drunken satyrs from her guest wing, framing the request as a favor between equals while making clear through subtle implication that refusal would be unwise. The satyrs were eventually evicted through a combination of beer, balcony-pushing, and redirection to a hag's hut, and Aurelian expressed satisfaction with the results while hinting that more services might be required.

What the party doesn't fully understand is that Aurelian is not merely a Feywild noble playing hostess—she is one of the anchors holding the fractured dimensions of the manor together, and her survival is essential to preventing complete planar collapse. The Corvinarus bloodline was grafted onto draconic power centuries ago, creating beings that exist partially outside normal reality and can serve as living keystones for dimensional architecture. Aurelian's presence in the Feywild reflection stabilizes that entire shard, just as other family members anchor other planes. If she dies, the Feywild manor collapses into the void, taking everyone inside with it.

This doesn't make her trustworthy. Aurelian's goals align with survival—her own first, the manor's second, everyone else's barely at all. She views the party as useful tools for solving problems she cannot address directly, and she will manipulate, deceive, and sacrifice them without hesitation if doing so serves her interests. Her delicate hostess persona is a carefully crafted mask designed to inspire protective instincts and underestimate her capabilities. In truth, she is a predator who has survived for centuries by appearing helpless while her enemies destroyed themselves.

The "delicate fairy" routine works because it contains elements of truth. Aurelian is genuinely constrained by the manor's dimensional instability, genuinely threatened by the forces that seek to sever the Corvinarus lineage, and genuinely dependent on others to handle problems that require leaving her chambers. But constrained is not the same as weak, and dependent is not the same as harmless. Those who mistake her circumstances for vulnerability tend not to survive the error.

Hjumpik's vision of the Grafting on Highsun 26 revealed the origin of Aurelian's power: an orange-robed figure cutting their palm over a screaming dragon egg in 988 BF, binding blood to blood and creating a lineage that would endure through dimensional catastrophe. What the vision didn't reveal is what that binding cost, what the dragon's screaming meant, or what happens to the bloodline when the last heir falls. Aurelian knows all of these things and shares none of them willingly. Information is power, and power is survival, and survival is everything.

The broken magic circle that Toad Lee discovered beneath her rug—the one requiring four days to repair, aligning with the end of the month—is Aurelian's project. She needs it functional to perform a ritual that will permanently stabilize her position in the Feywild shard, but she cannot complete the repairs herself due to restrictions on her movement and power. She is cultivating the party as repair crews, defenders, and eventual sacrifices, though she would phrase it more diplomatically if asked.
biography.public: A fey woman of impossible delicacy, with skin like porcelain and hair like autumn leaves, reclining on cushions in an overgrown bedroom. Her smile is warm and her eyes are old and something about her stillness suggests a predator waiting.

description.value:
A flowing gown in shades of orange, amber, and deep red that seems to shift and rustle like autumn leaves even when Aurelian is perfectly still. The fabric is not fabric at all but a manifestation of her connection to the seasonal aspect of the Feywild, leaves and petals and threads of pure fey magic woven into a garment that exists because she wills it to exist. If she died, the gown would crumble to autumn debris within seconds. If she removed it willingly, it would reform around her at her next thought. The gown is part of her in ways that mortal clothing cannot be.

The orange coloring is deliberate and symbolic—the signature of the Corvinarus bloodline since the Grafting in 988 BF, when the family bound itself to draconic power through rituals that stained their essence the color of fire and harvest. Every Corvinarus heir wears orange as a declaration of lineage and a warning to those who understand what the color means. In courts where memory is long, the orange gown opens doors that armies could not breach. In courts where memory has faded, it means nothing, and that difference tells Aurelian everything she needs to know about which courts still matter.

The gown provides a +2 bonus to AC (already calculated in her statistics) and grants Aurelian advantage on Charisma checks made to impress, intimidate, or seduce fey creatures. It also causes plants within 10 feet of her to slowly shift toward autumn coloring—leaves yellowing, flowers drooping, fruit ripening—a subtle effect that marks her presence even when she attempts to go unnoticed.
description.chat: The gown whispers with every movement, leaves that aren't quite leaves rustling with secrets in a language older than words.

unidentified.name: Impossible Autumn Gown
unidentified.description: A flowing gown in autumn colors that shifts and rustles without wind, the fabric appearing to be woven from actual leaves and petals that never wilt or fall. The garment seems less worn than manifested, existing as an extension of the wearer rather than a separate object. Plants nearby slowly change color in response to its presence.

description.value:
A heavy gold ring bearing the Corvinarus family seal: a stylized dragon coiled around a crown, rendered in orange enamel that seems to glow faintly from within. The ring has been passed through the family since the Grafting, each heir wearing it as proof of their position in the bloodline and their authority over family holdings across multiple dimensions. Aurelian received it from her mother—or the being she called mother—during a succession ritual that she does not discuss and that left her changed in ways that took decades to fully manifest.

The ring functions as a key to various Corvinarus holdings, allowing Aurelian to open doors that recognize family authority, command servants bound to the bloodline, and access resources cached across the manor's dimensional fragments. It also serves as a focusing device for the draconic power grafted into her lineage, allowing her to channel abilities that would otherwise require more elaborate ritual preparation. Without the ring, she would still possess her power, but accessing it would be slower and more costly.

The ring cannot be removed from Aurelian's finger by any means short of severing the finger or killing her. Previous heirs who attempted to pass it on prematurely discovered that the ring considers itself the arbiter of succession, not the wearer. Three would-be heirs died when the ring rejected their claims. Aurelian does not intend to be the fourth, which is one reason she's survived as long as she has.
description.chat: The orange enamel pulses like a heartbeat, the dragon's coils seeming to tighten around the crown with each passing moment.

unidentified.name: Noble's Signet Ring
unidentified.description: A heavy gold ring bearing an elaborate seal in glowing orange enamel—a dragon coiled around a crown. The ring sits on the wearer's finger with obvious permanence, showing no gap between metal and skin as though it grew there rather than being placed. Something about the design suggests authority of a kind that expects obedience.

description.value:
A delicate folding fan of orange silk stretched over ivory ribs, painted with scenes of autumn forests that shift slightly when viewed from different angles. Aurelian carries it constantly, using it to punctuate conversation, hide expressions, and direct attention with the practiced gestures of someone who learned fan language in courts where such skills were essential for survival. The fan is also a weapon, though not in any physical sense—the ivory ribs are sharp enough to cut, but Aurelian has never once used them for that purpose when magic serves better.

The fan amplifies Aurelian's enchantment magic, granting her advantage on spell attacks and increasing the save DC by 1 for any spell she casts while holding it that charms, frightens, or compels a creature. The amplification works through resonance with her nature rather than independent enchantment—the fan would be merely pretty in another's hands, but in hers it becomes an extension of her will.

Three times per day, Aurelian can flutter the fan while speaking a command and cast Suggestion without expending a spell slot. The command must be delivered as a whisper audible only to the target, and the target must be able to see the fan's movement. Aurelian uses this ability frequently for minor manipulations—servants who need redirecting, guests who need forgetting, problems that need solving without visible intervention.
description.chat: The fan flutters once, twice, and suddenly you're uncertain whether the thought you just had was yours or hers.

unidentified.name: Ornate Silk Fan
unidentified.description: A delicate folding fan of orange silk painted with shifting autumn scenes. The owner handles it with practiced grace, using gestures that seem to carry meaning beyond simple cooling. Something about watching the fan move makes it difficult to look away, difficult to think clearly, difficult to remember what you were going to say.

description.value:
Hidden beneath an ornate rug in Aurelian's overgrown Master Bedroom lies a magic circle that Toad Lee identified on Highsun 26 as requiring approximately four days to repair—a timeline that aligns suspiciously with the end of the month and whatever events the various factions are positioning themselves around. The circle is ancient, predating the current dimensional fracture, and was originally designed to perform rituals of stabilization and binding that would anchor the Corvinarus bloodline to specific planar coordinates.

The circle broke during the Shattered Ritual on Highsun 21, when the Oracle's failed synchronization rite sent shockwaves through all dimensional reflections of the manor. In the physical world, the ritual chamber collapsed. In the Shadowfell, reality fragmented into hostile shards. In the Feywild, the circle cracked, and Aurelian's ability to stabilize her domain cracked with it. She has been slowly dying ever since—not in any visible way, but in the gradual erosion of her connection to the Feywild shard, a loosening of the anchor that keeps her from drifting into the void between dimensions.

Repairing the circle requires specific materials, specific knowledge, and specific labor that Aurelian cannot provide herself. She has been gathering all three through manipulation of the manor's visitors, cultivating useful idiots who can perform the physical repairs while she provides guidance from her cushions. The party is her current best option, though she maintains backup plans involving the satyrs, the goblins, and at least one entity she has not yet revealed to anyone.

What Aurelian has not disclosed is what the repaired circle will actually do. She speaks of "stabilization" and "restoration," but the ritual she intends to perform will do more than anchor her to the Feywild shard. It will consume the dimensional energy of everyone present when the circle activates, feeding their existence to the Corvinarus bloodline and ensuring Aurelian's survival for another century. The party would be wise to investigate the circle's true purpose before the repairs are complete.
description.chat: The circle's lines glow faintly beneath the rug, broken geometry straining to reconnect, hungry for the power that will make it whole.

unidentified.name: Hidden Floor Circle
unidentified.description: A complex magical circle inscribed on the floor beneath a rug, its lines cracked and incomplete. The circle glows faintly with residual power, suggesting it was once functional and could be again with proper repairs. The geometry is unfamiliar, drawing on traditions that predate common magical practice.

description.value:
The pile of cushions where Aurelian reclines is not merely comfortable furniture but a manifestation of the constraints that bind her to the Master Bedroom. She cannot leave this room under her own power—the dimensional instability that followed the Shattered Ritual has locked her in place, making the cushions less a choice than a necessity elegantly disguised. She has arranged them artfully, surrounded them with drapery and faded grandeur, transformed her prison into a throne room, but the bars are no less real for being invisible.

The cushions themselves are unremarkable fey craftsmanship, woven from silk and stuffed with feathers from birds that no longer exist. They've been here for centuries, replaced and repaired by servants who understood their mistress's need for appearances even in captivity. Aurelian spends most of her time on these cushions, rarely moving more than a few feet from the pile's center, conserving the energy she cannot afford to waste on movement when survival requires every scrap of power focused on maintaining her connection to the shard.

Visitors who sit on the cushions without invitation discover that standing again is more difficult than expected—a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw is required to leave the cushion pile voluntarily, as Aurelian's ambient magic encourages guests to stay and talk rather than rush off before she's extracted everything useful from them. Aurelian is not consciously activating this effect; it simply happens around her, a predator's instinct made manifest in fey enchantment.
description.chat: The cushions embrace you with warmth that makes standing seem like such effort, surely there's time for one more question.

unidentified.name: Suspiciously Comfortable Cushions
unidentified.description: A pile of silk cushions arranged with obvious care, each one seeming softer and more inviting than the last. Sitting down feels like the obvious choice. Standing up feels like it can wait. Something about the arrangement suggests the cushions are meant to keep guests close rather than merely comfortable.

description.value:
A large portrait hangs on the wall of the Master Bedroom, depicting a family gathering across multiple generations of Corvinarus heirs. All wear orange. All have the same unsettling eyes—too bright, too knowing, with pupils that seem to follow viewers around the room. The painting's style shifts subtly from section to section, as though different artists painted different portions across centuries of additions, each new heir added to the canvas as they ascended.

Aurelian appears near the center of the portrait, looking much as she does now, surrounded by figures she identifies as her mother, her grandmother, and ancestors stretching back to the Grafting. The figure at the painting's edge, partially obscured by shadow, wears the orange robe seen in Hjumpik's vision—the original Corvinarus, the one who cut their palm over the screaming dragon egg and began everything that followed. That figure's face is not visible, painted in deliberate obscurity that no restoration has ever managed to clarify.

The portrait is more than decorative. It serves as a focus for Aurelian's awareness of other Corvinarus heirs across the dimensional shards—she can sense, dimly, when family members in other reflections of the manor are threatened or killed. The portrait showed her the Shadowfell heir's precarious position at Orangus Cornelius's dinner party. It showed her the physical manor's heir dying during the Shattered Ritual. It will show her if anyone attempts to harm the bloodline, and it will show her—eventually—who might be responsible.
description.chat: Eyes watch from the canvas, generations of orange-clad figures united in attention that feels less like paint and more like presence.

unidentified.name: Unsettling Family Portrait
unidentified.description: A large portrait depicting multiple generations of a noble family, all wearing variations of orange formal wear. The eyes of every figure seem to follow viewers, and the painting's style shifts subtly across its surface as though painted by different artists over a very long time. One figure at the edge is deliberately obscured, their face hidden in shadow that resists close examination.

description.value:
Aurelian is a 9th-level spellcaster using Charisma as her spellcasting ability (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). Her magic draws on both fey nature and the draconic power grafted into her bloodline, manifesting as a blend of enchantment, illusion, and elemental manipulation that reflects autumn's beauty and autumn's decay. Aurelian has the following spells prepared:

Cantrips (at will): Druidcraft, Friends, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation, Thaumaturgy

1st level (4 slots): Charm Person, Command, Disguise Self, Faerie Fire

2nd level (3 slots): Calm Emotions, Enthrall, Hold Person, Suggestion

3rd level (3 slots): Hypnotic Pattern, Major Image, Plant Growth

4th level (3 slots): Charm Monster, Dominate Beast, Greater Invisibility

5th level (1 slot): Dominate Person, Modify Memory

Aurelian's spell selection emphasizes control and manipulation over direct damage. She prefers to end conflicts before they begin through charm and misdirection, reserving combat magic for situations where subtlety has already failed. When forced to fight directly, she relies on Dominate effects to turn enemies against each other, using her own fragility as a weapon by forcing attackers to strike their allies instead.

Her use of Modify Memory deserves special note—Aurelian considers inconvenient truths to be problems with simple solutions, and she has no compunction about rewriting the memories of anyone who learns things she'd prefer they forget. The party should be aware that any private information shared in her presence may not remain private, and any agreements made may not be remembered as made.
description.chat: Magic flows through her like sap through autumn branches, sweet and slow and ultimately poisonous to anything that drinks too deep.

description.value:
In addition to her prepared spells, Aurelian can innately cast certain spells without material components, drawing on her fey nature and draconic heritage. Her innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 17). She can innately cast the following spells:

At will: Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Speak with Plants

3/day each: Dispel Magic, Fear, Misty Step

1/day each: Polymorph, Wall of Fire

The at-will abilities reflect Aurelian's constant awareness of her surroundings—she is always listening to the plants, always sensing surface thoughts, always alert for magical threats or opportunities. The daily abilities reveal her true nature more clearly: the fear she can inspire, the fire she inherited from draconic lineage, the transformative power that allows her to become something other than her usual delicate presentation when circumstances require.

Aurelian rarely uses Wall of Fire or Polymorph in view of guests, as these abilities contradict her carefully cultivated image of fragility. When she does use them, she prefers to ensure no witnesses survive to report what they saw. The party has not yet seen her use any innate ability beyond Detect Thoughts, which she employs constantly and without any indication that she's doing so.
description.chat: She doesn't gesture, doesn't speak, doesn't visibly do anything at all—and yet you feel magic moving around you like currents in deep water.

description.value:
Aurelian presents herself as a fragile fey noblewoman overwhelmed by circumstances beyond her control, and she plays this role with the skill of centuries of practice. Her voice is soft, her gestures delicate, her expressions carefully calibrated to inspire protective instincts in those who might otherwise recognize her as a threat. She asks for help rather than demanding it, frames requests as favors rather than commands, and never, ever reveals capability that would undermine her helpless presentation.

This persona grants Aurelian advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks to appear harmless, helpless, or in need of protection. Creatures who have not seen her use combat abilities or powerful magic must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom (Insight) check to recognize that her fragility is a performance rather than reality. Even after witnessing her true capabilities, observers tend to rationalize what they saw—surely she was desperate, surely those abilities cost her dearly, surely she's even more vulnerable now that she's been forced to reveal herself.

The persona is not entirely false. Aurelian is genuinely constrained by the dimensional instability, genuinely dependent on others for certain tasks, and genuinely at risk from forces that seek to destroy her bloodline. But constrained and dependent and at risk are not the same as weak, and those who treat her as truly helpless rarely survive long enough to learn the difference.
description.chat: She looks so fragile sitting there among the cushions, so in need of protection. It would be cruel not to help her. Wouldn't it?

description.value:
Aurelian's existence is bound to the Feywild reflection of the manor in ways that transcend normal occupancy. She is not merely living in this dimension—she is anchoring it, her presence serving as a keystone that prevents the Feywild shard from collapsing into the void between planes. If Aurelian dies, the entire Feywild reflection of the manor will destabilize within hours, eventually imploding and taking everyone inside with it.

This binding provides Aurelian with certain advantages within her domain. She is aware of significant events anywhere in the Feywild manor, sensing disturbances like a spider feeling vibrations in her web. She can communicate telepathically with any creature in the manor who has accepted her hospitality (including anyone who has eaten her food, drunk her wine, or accepted her direct invitation). And she cannot be forcibly removed from the manor by any means—teleportation effects, banishment, or physical ejection simply fail when attempted against her.

However, the binding also constrains her. She cannot leave the Master Bedroom without expending significant energy, and she cannot leave the manor at all under any circumstances. She is dependent on others to handle problems outside her immediate reach. And she must constantly maintain her connection to the shard, a drain on her resources that prevents her from operating at full magical capacity. In many ways, she is as much prisoner as ruler.
description.chat: She is the thread that keeps this reality woven, the weight that holds the shard in place. Without her, it all unravels.

description.value:
The Grafting of 988 BF bound the Corvinarus bloodline to draconic power, and that binding manifests in Aurelian as capabilities that contradict her fey appearance. She possesses resistance to cold, fire, and lightning damage—the elemental defenses of a dragon rather than a fey creature. Her eyes, when she allows them to show their true nature, have vertical pupils like a serpent's. And buried within her, accessible only in moments of extreme need, is the capacity for draconic fury that could transform her from delicate hostess to devastating combatant.

Aurelian rarely reveals these capabilities, as they contradict her carefully cultivated image. The resistance to damage she cannot hide—observant attackers will notice that fire and frost harm her less than expected—but she attributes this to "fey constitution" rather than draconic ancestry. The true nature of her eyes she conceals through constant minor illusion. And the draconic fury she has used exactly three times in the past century, each time in situations where no other option remained.

The heritage also connects her to dragons across the planes, though this connection has become strained since the revelation of the Dragon Conspiracy on Highsun 21. Aurelian knew that the war between dragons and the Regal Empire was a fabrication—the Corvinarus family has always known—but she maintained silence to preserve political options. Now that Robinson and Ignis-Major have exposed the truth, those options have narrowed, and Aurelian finds herself reassessing alliances that have stood for generations.
description.chat: For a moment—just a moment—her eyes flash with something older than fey, older than autumn, old as scales and fire and hoarded gold.

description.value:
Twice per day, when Aurelian fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead. This reflects both her fey resilience and the draconic power that reinforces her existence, allowing her to shrug off effects that would incapacitate lesser creatures. She uses this ability sparingly, conserving it for genuinely dangerous situations rather than minor inconveniences, but she has no hesitation about invoking it when her survival is at stake.

Each use of Legendary Resistance costs Aurelian energy she can ill afford to spare, weakening her connection to the dimensional anchor and forcing her to spend additional time recovering on her cushions. Those who force her to use this ability may notice that she seems slightly diminished afterward, her glow less bright, her presence less overwhelming. This is not performance—it is genuine cost, one more drain on reserves that grow thinner with each passing day.
description.chat: The spell should have worked. You watched it hit her. But she simply... doesn't allow it to take effect.

description.value: Aurelian makes two attacks with her Autumn's Touch or casts one spell and makes one Autumn's Touch attack.
description.chat: She moves with deceptive speed, each gesture carrying the weight of seasonal decay.

description.value:
Aurelian's primary physical attack manifests as a touch that carries the essence of autumn—the transition from life to death, the beauty of decay, the cold that precedes winter. Her hand seems to trail leaves and frost, and where she touches, living things wither. The attack deals necrotic damage as vitality drains away, and fire damage as the body burns through its own reserves trying to sustain itself.

Aurelian rarely uses this attack, as it contradicts her delicate hostess image and requires her to move from her cushions. When she does use it, she prefers to present the touch as a last resort, a desperate measure forced upon her by circumstances. In truth, she could have used it all along—she simply chooses not to until other options are exhausted or until she decides that maintaining her persona is less important than ending a threat quickly.

Creatures killed by Autumn's Touch decay rapidly, their bodies shriveling and browning like fallen leaves. Within hours, only fragments remain, soon scattered by any wind. This makes the attack useful for disposing of problems that Aurelian would prefer not to explain.
description.chat: Her fingers brush your skin, and suddenly you feel the cold of November, the weight of fading years, the beauty of things ending.

unidentified.name: Draining Touch
unidentified.description: This creature can deliver a touch attack that combines necrotic and fire damage, draining vitality and accelerating decay in targets.

description.value:
Aurelian can release a burst of autumn energy in a 30-foot radius centered on herself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 6d8 necrotic damage and has its hit point maximum reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken until it finishes a long rest. On a success, a creature takes half damage and suffers no hit point maximum reduction.

Simultaneously, plants in the area experience a full season cycle in seconds—budding, growing, fruiting, and dying—which Aurelian can shape to produce difficult terrain of fallen leaves and branches, or to create a single valuable fruit worth up to 50 gold pieces if harvested within one minute (after which it rots to nothing).

Aurelian uses this ability only when her survival is genuinely threatened, as it reveals capabilities she prefers to conceal and drains energy she cannot easily replace. Those who witness it rarely forget the sight: a delicate woman at the center of a sphere of death and decay, leaves swirling around her like a crown, her eyes finally showing their true nature as everything nearby withers and falls.
description.chat: Autumn erupts around her—not the gentle season but its truest meaning, the unstoppable death that follows harvest, the cold that follows warmth.

description.value:
For the duration, you sense the presence of magical effects within 30 feet of yourself. If you sense such effects, you can take the Magic action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears the magic, and if an effect was created by a spell, you learn the spell's school of magic.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

You activate one of the effects below. Until the spell ends, you can activate either effect as a Magic action on your later turns.

Sense Thoughts. You sense the presence of thoughts within 30 feet of yourself that belong to creatures that know languages or are telepathic. You don't read the thoughts, but you know that a thinking creature is present.

The spell is blocked by 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood; 1 inch of metal; or a thin sheet of lead.

Read Thoughts. Target one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself or one creature within 30 feet of yourself that you detected with the Sense Thoughts option. You learn what is most on the target's mind right now. If the target doesn't know any languages and isn't telepathic, you learn nothing.

As a Magic action on your next turn, you can try to probe deeper into the target's mind. If you probe deeper, the target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you discern the target's reasoning, emotions, and something that looms large in its mind (such as a worry, love, or hate). On a successful save, the spell ends. Either way, the target knows that you are probing into its mind, and until you shift your attention away from the target's mind, the target can take an action on its turn to make an [[/check ability=int skill=arc dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC, ending the spell on a success.

You imbue plants in an immobile 30-foot Emanation with limited sentience and animation, giving them the ability to communicate with you and follow your simple commands. You can question plants about events in the spell's area within the past day, gaining information about creatures that have passed, weather, and other circumstances.

You can also turn &Reference[difficultterrain] caused by plant growth (such as thickets and undergrowth) into ordinary terrain that lasts for the duration. Or you can turn ordinary terrain where plants are present into Difficult Terrain that lasts for the duration.

The spell doesn't enable plants to uproot themselves and move about, but they can move their branches, tendrils, and stalks for you.

If a Plant creature is in the area, you can communicate with it as if you shared a common language.

Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Any ongoing spell of level 3 or lower on the target ends. For each ongoing spell of level 4 or higher on the target, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability (DC 10 plus that spell's level). On a successful check, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You automatically end a spell on the target if the spell's level is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot you use.

Each creature in a 30-foot Cone must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or drop whatever it is holding and have the &Reference[frightened apply=false] condition for the duration.

A Frightened creature takes the &Reference[dash] action and moves away from you by the safest route on each of its turns unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a space where it doesn't have line of sight to you, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends on that creature.

effects.name: Fear
effects.description: A &Reference[frightened apply=false] creature takes the &Reference[dash] action and moves away from you by the safest route on each of its turns unless there is nowhere to move. If the creature ends its turn in a space where it doesn’t have line of sight to you, the creature makes a [[/save ability=wis]] saving throw. On a successful save, the spell ends on that creature.

description.value: Briefly surrounded by silvery mist, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

You attempt to transform a creature that you can see within range into a Beast. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or shape-shift into a Beast form for the duration. That form can be any Beast you choose that has a Challenge Rating equal to or less than the target's (or the target's level if it doesn't have a Challenge Rating). The target's game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the chosen Beast, but the target retains its alignment, personality, creature type, Hit Points, and Hit Point Dice. See appendix B for a sample of Beast stat blocks.

The target gains a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to the Hit Points of the Beast form. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the spell ends. The spell ends early on the target if it has no Temporary Hit Points left.

The target is limited in the actions it can perform by the anatomy of its new form, and it can't speak or cast spells.

The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

You create a wall of fire on a solid surface within range. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and lasts for the duration.

When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d8 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

One side of the wall, selected by you when you cast this spell, deals 5d8 Fire damage to each creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side or inside the wall. A creature takes the same damage when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The other side of the wall deals no damage.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 4.

Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range.

Weather Sensor. You create a Tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 round.

Bloom. You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.

Sensory Effect. You create a harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, spectral dancing fairies, a gentle breeze, the sound of an animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot Cube.

Fire Play. You light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a campfire.

Target a Beast that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition for the duration. If you or one of your allies deals damage to the target, the spells ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can target one additional Beast for each spell slot level above 1.

effects.name: Charmed

description.value:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. See the descriptions below for the effects of each. The illusion ends if you cast this spell again.

If a creature takes a Study action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

Sound. If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

Image. If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot Cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, since things can pass through it.

You create a magical effect within range. Choose the effect from the options below. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time.

Sensory Effect. You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

Fire Play. You instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.

Clean or Soil. You instantaneously clean or soil an object no larger than 1 cubic foot.

Minor Sensation. You chill, warm, or flavor up to 1 cubic foot of nonliving material for 1 hour.

Magic Mark. You make a color, a small mark, or a symbol appear on an object or a surface for 1 hour.

Minor Creation. You create a nonmagical trinket or an illusory image that can fit in your hand. It lasts until the end of your next turn. A trinket can deal no damage and has no monetary worth.

You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on [[/check ability=cha skill=itm]] checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or follow the command on its next turn. Choose the command from these options:

Approach. The target moves toward you by the shortest and most direct route, ending its turn if it moves within 5 feet of you.

Drop. The target drops whatever it is holding and then ends its turn.

Flee. The target spends its turn moving away from you by the fastest available means.

Grovel. The target has the Prone condition and then ends its turn.

Halt. On its turn, the target doesn't move and takes no action or Bonus Action.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can affect one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

You make yourself—including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings on your person—look different until the spell ends. You can seem 1 foot shorter or taller and can appear heavier or lighter. You must adopt a form that has the same basic arrangement of limbs as you have. Otherwise, the extent of the illusion is up to you.

The changes wrought by this spell fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, if you use this spell to add a hat to your outfit, objects pass through the hat, and anyone who touches it would feel nothing.

To discern that you are disguised, a creature must take the Study action to inspect your appearance and succeed on an [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC.

For the duration, objects and affected creatures shed &Reference[dimlight] in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition.

Attack rolls against an affected creature or object have Advantage if the attacker can see it.

  • The creature has Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions until the spell ends. If the creature was already Charmed or Frightened, those conditions are suppressed for the duration.
  • The creature becomes Indifferent about creatures of your choice that it's Hostile toward. This indifference ends if the target takes damage or witnesses its allies taking damage. When the spell ends, the creature's attitude returns to normal.

You suggest a course of activity—described in no more than 25 words—to one creature you can see within range that can hear and understand you. The suggestion must sound achievable and not involve anything that would obviously deal damage to the target or its allies. For example, you could say, "Fetch the key to the cult's treasure vault, and give the key to me." Or you could say, "Stop fighting, leave this library peacefully, and don't return."

The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed condition for the duration or until you or your allies deal damage to the target. The Charmed target pursues the suggestion to the best of its ability. The suggested activity can continue for the entire duration, but if the suggested activity can be completed in a shorter time, the spell ends for the target upon completing it.

You create a twisting pattern of colors in a 30-foot Cube within range. The pattern appears for a moment and vanishes. Each creature in the area who can see the pattern must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[charmed apply=false] condition for the duration. While Charmed, the creature has the &Reference[incapacitated apply=false] condition and a Speed of 0.

The spell ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage or if someone else uses an action to shake the creature out of its stupor.

You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 20-foot Cube. The image appears at a spot that you can see within range and lasts for the duration. It seems real, including sounds, smells, and temperature appropriate to the thing depicted, but it can't deal damage or cause conditions.

If you are within range of the illusion, you can take a Magic action to cause the image to move to any other spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking. Similarly, you can cause the illusion to make different sounds at different times, even making it carry on a conversation, for example.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, for things can pass through it. A creature that takes a Study action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful [[/check ability=int skill=inv dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image, and its other sensory qualities become faint to the creature.

Casting Time: Action (Overgrowth) or 8 hours (Enrichment)

This spell channels vitality into plants. The casting time you use determines whether the spell has the Overgrowth or the Enrichment effect below.

Overgrowth. Choose a point within range. All normal plants in a 100-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point become thick and overgrown. A creature moving through that area must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves. You can exclude one or more areas of any size within the spell's area from being affected.

Enrichment. All plants in a half-mile radius centered on a point within range become enriched for 365 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested. They can benefit from only one Plant Growth per year.

You have a telepathic link with the Charmed target while the two of you are on the same plane of existence. On your turn, you can use this link to issue commands to the target (no action required), such as "Attack that creature," "Move over there," or "Fetch that object." The target does its best to obey on its turn. If it completes an order and doesn't receive further direction from you, it acts and moves as it likes, focusing on protecting itself.

You can command the target to take a Reaction but must take your own Reaction to do so.

You attempt to reshape another creature's memories. One creature that you can see within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. If you are fighting the creature, it has Advantage on the save. On a failed save, the target has the &Reference[Charmed apply=false] condition for the duration. While Charmed in this way, the target also has the &Reference[Incapacitated apply=false] condition and is unaware of its surroundings, though it can hear you. If it takes any damage or is targeted by another spell, this spell ends, and no memories are modified.

While this charm lasts, you can affect the target's memory of an event that it experienced within the last 24 hours and that lasted no more than 10 minutes. You can permanently eliminate all memory of the event, allow the target to recall the event with perfect clarity, change its memory of the event's details, or create a memory of some other event.

You must speak to the target to describe how its memories are affected, and it must be able to understand your language for the modified memories to take root. Its mind fills in any gaps in the details of your description. If the spell ends before you finish describing the modified memories, the creature's memory isn't altered. Otherwise, the modified memories take hold when the spell ends.

A modified memory doesn't necessarily affect how a creature behaves, particularly if the memory contradicts the creature's natural inclinations, alignment, or beliefs. An illogical modified memory, such as a false memory of how much the creature enjoyed swimming in acid, is dismissed as a bad dream. The DM might deem a modified memory too nonsensical to affect a creature.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. You can alter the target's memories of an event that took place up to 7 days ago (level 6 spell slot), 30 days ago (level 7 spell slot), 365 days ago (level 8 spell slot), or any time in the creature's past (level 9 spell slot).
